idiom_name: composed DBIO batch run inside transactionally (Slick), ConnectionIO.transact (doobie)
implementation_notes: Slick models database work as DBIOAction values: rows += row describes a statement rather than executing it, nothing runs until db.run(action), and .transactionally makes the whole composed action atomic at that point; doobie's ConnectionIO programs are equivalent in spirit (transact runs the program at the end). The deferral to a boundary is therefore explicit, but no identity-keyed dirty tracking exists, so the change set must be collected by hand and turned into a batch of actions. What replaces the classic structure: action-as-value composition with an explicit transaction combinator; justified when the writes are naturally batched.
code_sketch:
val updates = records.map(r => authors.insertOrUpdate(r))
val program = DBIO.sequence(updates).transactionally   // nothing yet
// ... collect more changes, then a single boundary call:
db.run(program).map(_ => ())   // all writes execute here, one transaction
pitfalls: A huge DBIO.sequence holds every action in memory and hits JDBC batch limits - chunk it into bounded batches.
transactionally only takes effect on the outermost action; nested actions run in auto-commit without savepoints.
A single failing action aborts the whole sequence, so batch a whole identity set only when you can retry it as a unit.
